text: Tilea is a thriving land of arts, trade, visionaries, tyrants, princes, cuisine, mercenaries and, most importantly at this point, divisions. A country born from the ruins of elven colonies, Tilea has never known unity since then, outside of short-lived and individualistic bursts, so that each of the richest and most powerful settlements are in fact autonomous city-states that usually respond quite violently at any external approach of assimilation. It is in a somewhat vicious cycle that tilean warriors are among the best in the Old World, since they are either used to perpetrate the state of division or to otherwise shift huge economical and political assets around.-Cataph

Estalia is founded on rivalry. Between Magritta and Bilbali, between the Inquisition and the other powers, with the Tileans, with the Bretonnians, with the Sultans of Araby. If one were to be able to put it on talking terms, perhaps even the Lustrian jungles would agree that, yes, there is a strong rivalry between its unforgiving tendrils and the estalian explorers. However, such relationships can be the base of something extremely wealthy: competition. And upon competition, with the due resources and willpower, a powerful nation can be bred and built, forged in fire and steel, if necessary.-Cataph

Perhaps not a single dweller of the Borderlands would agree to admit it, but the humans of this country are like a large, robust creeper. Centuries ago, human colonists and refugees started to built a new nation on the borders of the Old World. Anyone else would have been strangled between mountain and sea, between Dwarfs and Greenskins. The men of the Borderlands endured the challenge and survive, perhaps in tides and ebbs when the green menace hits harder, but survive nonetheless, without the immense manpower of the Empire, the natural resilience of the Dwarfs, the blessings of the Bretonnians or the wisdom of the High Elves. The men of the Borderlands fight for their hardened pride and their homes.-Cataph
